title: Spatiotemporal Non-Hermitian Skin Effect with Floquet-Engineered Ultracold Atoms
authors: Weijie Liang, Weiping Zhang, Keye Zhang
abstract: Non-Hermitian skin effect, the accumulation of bulk eigenstates at edges under open boundary conditions, has been observed across classical, quantum, and synthetic platforms. Whether it can be generalized to the genuine time dimension remains open. We propose a spatiotemporal NHSE in the Floquet phase space via Floquet engineering of a ring-trapped ultracold atomic gas. Placing spatial and temporal degrees of freedom on an equal footing, we show that a single parent skin effect projects onto either domain. The spatial projection yields an NHSE with arbitrarily tunable skin locations, eliminating the need for physical open boundaries. The temporal projection gives time-domain nonreciprocity and periodic temporal funneling, consistent with causality. This establishes a unified spatiotemporal paradigm for NHSE and opens a route to non-Hermitian topological physics in time.
summary: This paper pioneers the concept of spatiotemporal Non-Hermitian Skin Effect (NHSE) using ultracold atoms driven by time-periodic potentials. By mapping the system dynamics into a Floquet phase space, the authors show that the NHSE can be engineered by coupling spatial and temporal degrees of freedom. This opens a powerful, boundary-free route to studying non-Hermitian topology in time.
main_problem: The primary goal is to generalize the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect (NHSE) from spatial dimensions to the genuine spatiotemporal domain.
main_result: The authors establish a unified spatiotemporal paradigm for NHSE using Floquet engineering, demonstrating that the effect manifests as time-domain nonreciprocity and periodic temporal funneling.
method: The study employs a semiclassical Floquet-phase-space (FPS) approach, deriving effective Hamiltonians and analyzing the resulting complex energy spectra under both periodic and open boundary conditions.
model_or_system: The system utilizes an ultracold atomic gas trapped in a ring and subjected to time-periodic driving potentials (Floquet engineering). The dynamics are analyzed by mapping the system onto the FPS, which treats time as a synthetic spatial dimension.
key_observables: Time-domain nonreciprocity, periodic temporal funneling, complex energy spectra loops, and the tunability of skin locations.
important_parameters: Dissipation ($\gamma$), geometric phase ($\Phi$), and the driving frequency ($\Omega$).
main_assumptions: Interatomic collisions are neglected, and the analysis relies on specific approximations like the secular approximation and the tight-binding description in the FPS.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the physical setup (ring trap), the synthesized zigzag ladder in the FPS, and dynamics showing probability accumulation (spatial projection) and time-domain funneling (temporal projection).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first introducing the concept of spatiotemporal NHSE, deriving the effective Hamiltonian in the FPS, and then analyzing the consequences of non-zero geometric phase and dissipation on both spatial and temporal projections.
why_interesting: This work directly applies advanced concepts from non-Hermitian physics (NHSE) to a highly controllable, state-of-the-art platform (ultracold atoms), providing a novel route to engineering time-dependent topological phenomena.
